.engine/operations/boot-session-start.md.why: boot-session-start is the heaviest member of the orientation family — the SessionStart pack a cold session is meant to read in full, every boot. Its length is load-bearing operator-facing content: the anti-habituation collapse rules and the repair-offer contracts in Notes, each a real behavior carrying its own tool name, loss semantics, and issue/decision reference, none redundant with another. When the 150 ceiling was set the repair set held five contracts (un-stranding, catch-up, off-main return, stranded-pull-request reconcile, branch-protection re-enable) at 121 body lines; it has since grown to ten — adding fresh-copy setup (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#353), engine-mechanic product-checkout orientation, half-finished-upgrade finish/undo (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#594), leftover-template-license clear/keep (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#471), and greenfield-intake offer/dismiss (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#553). That is genuine capability growth, not the repetition issue StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#364 trimmed. This session first trimmed the real over-narration — the per-bullet restatements of the shared repair-offer preamble, a duplicated read-only-of-canonical-state refinement, and the anti-habituation prose — landing the file at 184 body lines, then raised the ceiling to 200 for the load-bearing remainder. The 200 ceiling is the operator's deliberate choice, set with durable headroom so the next repair contract does not force another guarded edit in a later session. It is still a ceiling, not a removal: the soft nudge fires again above 200, and this rule's hard tier still fails a malformed or reasonless override, so a dead grant cannot silently accumulate. The raise lives in this guarded rule, so it needs the operator's deliberate sign-off — the recorded-reason pattern issue StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#273 asked for, and the resolution of issue StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#460 (a recorded ceiling rather than a runbook silently sitting over budget, or its load-bearing prose shaved to fit). Raised again 2026-09-04, from 200 to 260, by the operator's typed ruling when authorizing the Build of plan pln_b8e8c727f6ed (typed lifecycle transactions part C, StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#821): that Build makes this length tier a hard merge block and re-measures every operation the way the hardened rule counts — body lines after the frontmatter with fenced blocks and generated regions excluded — and boot-session-start measured 258 under that count. Its growth since the 200 ceiling is the same kind as before: additional repair-offer contracts and the typed session-start relay, each a real behavior a cold session must read in full, not repetition. Trimming 58 lines would cut those contracts, so the operator chose a ceiling over a trim; 260 is two lines above the measurement, deliberately tight, so any further growth returns to the operator as a guarded edit rather than accumulating silently. This is the single ceiling raise that Build grants; every other over-budget operation in the same audit was trimmed to fit.

.engine/operations/plan-orchestration.md.why: plan-orchestration is the judgment half of the plan lifecycle — the deliberative protocol a session answers before authoring, the operator's stops in order, the four entry doors, and the seams (the local plan library, the shelf moments, the seal's hand-back, and the bind seam downstream). It deliberately restates none of the Project Manager's verb sequence, which the tool itself owns and self-guides, so its length is judgment prose rather than mechanics duplicated from code. The operator priced this ceiling as a SWAP rather than a grant (2026-08-27, StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#1097 finding 1): the raise was conditional on build-orchestration.md shedding body lines in the same change, with plan-side prose relocated and anything parroting runtime guidance the tool prints deleted in transit rather than moved. The estimate was 50. Executing the swap measured 35, and reaching 50 would have meant cutting Build-side discipline instead — so the operator re-priced mid-Build at what the swap bought. Then a deliverable reviewer found that even 35 had taken Build-side rules with it (the cold-handoff mechanics and the snapshot's data-minimisation rule, restored in the same change), leaving the honest figure at 27. This ceiling is the operator's third and deliberate answer to that measurement: 150, six lines above where the runbook actually ships, chosen so a file this size is not one sentence from its cap while staying near what the trade bought. The same decision holds build-orchestration's own line and word ratchets at its exact measurement, so the traded lines cannot be quietly refilled. It is still a ceiling, not a removal: the soft nudge fires again above 150, and this rule's hard tier still fails a malformed or reasonless override, so a dead grant cannot silently accumulate.

.engine/operations/build-orchestration.m.why: build-orchestration remains the convergence runbook for planning, review, implementation, validation, repair, and submission, but the mechanical Build coordinator now carries repeatable state and evidence handling that previously required extensive procedural narration here. The reconstructed runbook is 221 prose-body lines: the 120-line default would still crowd its responsibility boundary, plan-storage rules, two review gates, proportional repair judgment, and human merge gate, while 250 leaves modest headroom without preserving the obsolete 450-line grant sized for the former 392-line procedure. This is the operator's deliberate post-reconstruction ceiling choice; the soft nudge fires above 250 and the rule's hard tier still rejects a malformed or reasonless override.

.engine/operations/memory-migration-tria.why: memory-migration-trial is the operator-attended go/no-go for replacing native memory with ClawMem (program prg_13dc60836f68, PR 2's gate), and almost every body line is SAFETY content that must not be shaved to fit a budget: what consenting to a cleartext export of private history means (with the scrub's deliberate exclusions — names, emails, phone numbers left intact — stated plainly), the three destination dangers the exporter's git guard cannot see (cloud-sync, network mounts, backup sweeps), the pre-registration discipline that keeps the verdict from being reverse-fitted, the dual-system battery and fixed pass bar, the committed verdict slot that binds five identities, and the residue-deletion step that removes the cleartext when the trial ends. Trimming any of these to reach 120 would cut a real control. The doc ships at 120 body lines; 160 is the operator's deliberate ceiling, chosen with headroom so filling in the verdict slot and the occasional clarification do not force a guarded edit in a later session. It is still a ceiling, not a removal: the soft nudge fires again above 160, and this rule's hard tier still fails a malformed or reasonless override, so a dead grant cannot silently accumulate.

message: An operation (a runbook under .engine/operations/) must contain, as level-2 headings in this order, Purpose, then Steps, then Done when, and it may also contain a Notes section, and no others. These sections are what make a runbook followable — what it is for, the ordered steps, and how to know it is done — so an operation that omits a required one is structurally incomplete. This check catches a broken SHAPE only: that the required sections are present, correctly ordered, and that no stray section appears. It cannot judge whether a section's content is substantive — an empty or hand-wavy section passes here and is caught instead by the operator reviewing the committed change, and whether the runbook actually tells a cold operator how to perform the procedure is the audits layer's judgment, not this check's. Length is checked too, at this rule's {length_tier} length tier: an operation's prose body — the lines after its frontmatter, with fenced code blocks and generated regions left out of the count — must stay within its line budget, which is {default_budget} lines by default and {effective_budget} for this operation (a specific operation may carry a higher recorded budget in length_budget_overrides, with the operator's reason). A malformed or stale override entry — one missing its budget or recorded reason, or naming no operation — is the rule's hard tier, so a dead budget grant cannot accumulate. Add or reorder the flagged sections to match the operation template (.engine/templates/operation.md) before merging.
